newsitem.title: CANADA: ICE HOCKEY-U.S. TEAM TURNS TABLES ON CANADA AT WORLD CUP.
newsitem.headline: ICE HOCKEY-U.S. TEAM TURNS TABLES ON CANADA AT WORLD CUP.

text.p: The United States' shocking 5-2 win over Canada on Saturday gave the Americans the World Cup championship two games to one and turned the world of ice hockey upside down.
"This is the best American team ever," said U.S. head coach Ron Wilson, whose regular job is coaching the National Hockey League's Anaheim Mighty Ducks.
"Twenty guys came together and withstood the pressures of an entire nation. We literally beat all of Canada's 28 million people."
Wayne Gretzky, Canada's captain and spiritual leader, admitted, "The loss is devastating. It's a crushed locker room and probably a crushed country. Hockey is our game and we were expected to win."

Gretzky, 35 and a recent free agent signee with the New York Rangers, missed a cross ice pass in the final minute when the U.S. team led just 3-2. He had an open shot to the net, but fell reaching for the puck.
That miss, and that defeat may hasten change at the top of hockey's world order.

"Canada used to have about 99 percent of the employment in the NHL, now they have about two thirds," said Lou Lamoriello, the general manager of the New Jersey Devils, who served in the same capacity with the U.S. team.
"There are about 125 Europeans in the NHL, including 60 Russians. We have about 50 Americans, although the number keeps changing.
"Nonetheless, from the beginning of this World Cup play the United States has been the best team. We proved it in the last four minutes with four goals."
The World Cup was staged jointly by the International Ice Hockey Federation, the NHL Players Association and the NHL and is a precursor to the 1998 Winter Olympics at Nagano, Japan.
At that time the NHL will shut down for two weeks and make their players available to their respective countries.
In the World Cup, the European Pool had Sweden, Finland, Germany and the Czech Republic, mostly staffed by NHL players. Sweden lost a semifinal double overtime match to Canada 3-2.
Peter Forsberg, one of Sweden's best players, said: "We won the 1994 Winter Olympics (on Forsberg's shoot out goal), by beating a Canadian team that didn't have all the top players.
"The gap between the European countries and Canada has closed. Sweden could have beaten this Canadian team with all their great players."
Glen Sather, the Edmonton Oilers general manager and coach of Canada, said: "The U.S. had the best goalie, the best defence and the best team."
David Ogrean, executive director of USA Hockey, said: "It is our biggest win since the gold medal at Lake Placid in 1980. Within the hockey community this win is just as important."

Canada had the pressure of an entire country on their team, Germany surprised with a trip to the semifinal, while the highly skilled Russian team disappointed, losing twice to the United States and once to Canada.
The level of competition excited NHL Commissioner Gary Bettman, who has high hopes for hockey's coming out party at the Nagano Olympics.
"Nagano will give hockey unsurpassed exposure," said Bettman. "Unlike the United States (basketball) Dream Team, we will have six dream teams, and no one knows who will win."
Pat LaFontaine, who played with the U.S. Olympic team at Sarajevo in 1984, said: "When Amonte scored (the go-ahead goal in the final) you could hear the silence.
"This made up for 16 years of not being good enough. To do this at this level, against Canada in Montreal, proves we are the best."
